definitions.explanation: The process of making information, data, processes, or problems that are normally hidden or abstract into a form that can be easily seen and understood. A business and management buzzword that became widely adopted in the 2000s.

examples.japanese: ⟦データ→データ：03944_deeta⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{見|み}える{化|か}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧だ。
examples.english: We need to visualize the data.

examples.japanese: ⟦{業務|ぎょうむ}→業務：09630_gyoumu⟧⟦プロセス→プロセス：11291_purosesu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{見|み}える{化|か}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: We will visualize the work processes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{在庫|ざいこ}→在庫：04701_zaiko⟧⟦{管理|かんり}→管理：00178_kanri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{見|み}える{化|か}⟦によって→によって：06801_niyotte⟧、⟦{無駄|むだ}→無駄：02512_muda⟧な⟦コスト→コスト：06666_kosuto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{削減|さくげん}→削減：11789_sakugen⟧⟦できた→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: By visualizing inventory management, we were able to reduce unnecessary costs.

notes:
Coined from the potential form of ⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧ (to see) — ⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧ (to be visible) — plus ⟦{化|か}→〜化：28335_ka⟧ (the suffix meaning "-ization"). The term originated in Toyota's manufacturing philosophy and spread widely into general business Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦データ→データ：03944_deeta⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{見|み}える{化|か}: data visualization
- ⟦{業務|ぎょうむ}→業務：09630_gyoumu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{見|み}える{化|か}: work process visualization
- ⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{見|み}える{化|か}: making problems visible
- ⟦{進捗|しんちょく}→進捗：07377_shinchoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{見|み}える{化|か}: progress visualization
- ⟦コスト→コスト：06666_kosuto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{見|み}える{化|か}: cost transparency

USAGE:
Originally a manufacturing concept associated with Toyota Production System, now used broadly in business, IT, and government contexts. It emphasizes making the invisible visible — not just displaying data, but structuring it so that problems and inefficiencies become immediately apparent.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{可視化|かしか}→可視化：07644_kashika⟧: visualization — more formal and technical; used in scientific and academic contexts
- {見|み}える{化|か}: visualization — more colloquial and business-oriented; emphasizes practical transparency
